title: Riska’s Study Time 2
text: “Ha, seems like even Itsuki got a bit drunk on the misfortune he witnessed, huh… well, I suppose if he’s recovered enough to talk about it with a laugh, that means he’s made some progress toward healing.” I continued the story, mocking myself a little as I went.
Eventually… he apparently woke up to a chilly sensation, I say.
“Ngh…”
“Are you awake?”

Blinking a few times through his hazy vision, once his sight finally cleared, what came into view was a Mole beastman cradling his head in her lap and tending to his wounds. Itsuki had half-hoped the events up to now had all been a dream, but as he looked around, he understood anew that he was locked in a cell within some noble’s mansion.
“I managed to stop the bleeding and give first aid, but…”
“You are…”
“I am… Emia Nilwen Riscela Teleti Coalies. Like you, I was brought here as a slave.”

Still half-conscious, Itsuki spoke while being nursed by the Mole he’d just met, I say. Being tended to, and having someone listen to him all the way through, made Itsuki feel a kindness he hadn’t felt in a long while, and he wept. The Mole gently let him rest his head on her lap and lulled him to sleep. From then on, it seems, the days that followed were nothing but torture.
“There! Lady Ivyred, you too shall deliver a holy blow of atonement upon these sinful devils!”
“I refuse! No matter what happens, I will never do such a thing!”

Incidentally, Riska—who had shielded Itsuki—was summoned day after day to the torture sessions and ordered to wield the whip herself, but each time, she refused loudly. It seemed this noble was trying to teach Riska the “joy” of tormenting beastmen as some kind of amusement. You know the type—refuse at first, but gradually get drawn in until there’s no escape. That sort of thing. But Riska never gave in, no matter what, standing firm and unbending even as she herself was whipped for it, and the noble was apparently quite irritated by this. Itsuki said it was precisely because of Riska’s courageous stance that he was able to believe justice still existed somewhere in this world.
“Stubborn wretch!”
Since Riska refused no matter what, she was eventually dragged off to another room, I say. When the noble returned, he inflicted even harsher torture on Itsuki, whipping included.
“Aaaaaahhhh!?”
“Hmph! Scream louder!”
“P-please, Itsuki-san hasn’t recovered his strength yet! He’ll die if this continues!”
“Silence! Hmph! Then it’s your turn next, for speaking out of line! Don’t think you’ll get off easy!”
“V-very well! I’ll take his share as well!”

Standing up sharply, Itsuki—who had felt a quiet relief at being freed from the pain—later admitted he’d been ashamed of himself for that very feeling. But having been abused to the point where he couldn’t even move, Itsuki could only writhe in agony, sprawled on the floor of the cell.
“Ugh, uuh… Emia-san. I’m… sorry.”

The Mole said nothing, only smiled gently at Itsuki’s hoarse voice and shook her head. It’s fine, you did nothing wrong—that was the feeling her expression conveyed, and it brought Itsuki to tears, or so he said.
“What foolish little farce are you beastmen putting on!”
Crackling with sparks, the noble activated the slave crest and throttled the Mole.
“Aaaaaaaahhhhh—!?”
“Hmph! Showing me such an unpleasant sight! You’d best prepare for a long night!”

And so, right before Itsuki’s eyes, the torment of the Mole continued on and on. Tortured until she was battered and broken, the Mole was nearly out of breath, but she endured it all the same, and the two of them were left sprawled together on the cell floor.
“Uu, Emi… a-san…”
“Ha, haha… are you… all right, Itsuki-san…”

Why did it have to be like this—Itsuki, so consumed by despair over his current situation that he nearly forgot everything that had come before, found his mind filled entirely with thoughts of the Mole who had taken on his share of the torment. The Mole’s fur was matted and disheveled, her body covered in countless wounds. Of course, Itsuki was in much the same state, terribly weakened. Whenever he tried to use magic, his throat would constrict, preventing him from casting it. At the very least, he thought, and using the compounding skill available to his bow, he produced medicine and rolled it over to the Mole.
“It’s… wound medicine. Please, use it.”

With the noble gone for now, Itsuki figured he needed to make use of whatever resources he had to heal even a little. The Mole took the wound medicine that rolled over to her and, with her weakened body, began applying it to Itsuki’s wounds instead.
“N-not me, you first.”
“It’s fine…”

The medicine took effect swiftly, and Itsuki’s wounds gradually began to heal. But it couldn’t restore his stamina. After finishing tending to Itsuki, the Mole used what little medicine remained to treat a small portion of her own wounds.
“Why… when your wounds are so much worse than mine…”
Itsuki asked this, having lost half his tail but otherwise being nowhere near as badly off as the Mole.
“I don’t want to be afraid anymore, or run away anymore…”
“What do you mean by that…”

“When a band of slave hunters attacked the settlement I lived in, everyone was killed or taken away. In the midst of it all… I trembled in fear and could do nothing while I watched my family being killed right in front of me.”
The Mole’s eyes grew distant as she spoke of her regret.

“I couldn’t do anything for the child crying in front of me, watching their family, their parents, being killed. That child’s mother was pregnant, and her belly was torn open right before our eyes… So now, if there’s someone suffering in front of me, and I can take their place, that’s enough for me. That’s all I need.”

That was the reality of slave hunting, as told by the Mole—and Itsuki realized just how arrogant he had been, up until now. Of course he’d intended to abolish this whole slavery system, and to punish those who used slaves. But the fact that slave hunters could do something so tragic had always felt like someone else’s problem to him. Since slavery had existed back on Earth too, he’d figured it wasn’t so strange for a fantasy world with magic to have something similar—that had been the extent of his understanding, shallow as it was. He’d never even been able to imagine how the people actually living through it thought, or felt, or survived.

What a naive sense of justice he’d been living by… and at the same time, he found himself deeply moved by the heart of this Mole, who wished to save others even before herself. Eventually, after finishing her care of Itsuki, the Mole pressed her hands together and prayed to the sky.
“Please, may Shield Hero-sama save us from tragedies such as this…”

Through the Mole’s prayer, Itsuki seemed to finally understand what a hero meant in this world. And at the same time, he came to understand just how much hope the demi-humans and beastmen placed in Naofumi, Shield Hero, and how the people of this country were trying to trample that hope underfoot. Yes—for the suffering demi-humans and beastmen, Shield Hero was their hope… and if that hero could be painted as a wicked, inhuman man, that alone would be enough to crush their hope. That was precisely why Shield Hero had to be made into a villain. Itsuki recalled the duel, and the faces of Crimson Swine and Trash floated up in his mind. I see… so that’s what humans are capable of.

‘I’m telling you, it’s about time you saw with your own eyes what kind of country this really is. It’s easy, and fun, isn’t it, to blame someone. If you’re truly a hero, shouldn’t you be more compassionate?’
Rabbit Guy’s words had pierced deep, deep into Itsuki’s chest. And then, Father’s words came next.

‘It means exactly what I said. Do you know? There’s a saying that humans become most cruel when they’re convinced they’re righteous. After all, once you’re certain you’re in the right, you believe anything is forgivable. That kind of certainty is what makes people capable of endless brutality.’

Itsuki came to understand, in his very bones, the cruelty of those who were convinced that tormenting demi-humans and beastmen was justice. Father ran a slave trade. The slaves who genuinely adored Father—their affection, surely, was real, heartfelt. The slave crest carved into the Mole’s body didn’t react to her speaking ill of the noble. Itsuki had always assumed that slave crests functioned something close to brainwashing—that they forced obedience to one’s master’s will, whether one wanted to speak against it or not. That had been his vague, unexamined assumption. Incidentally, it seemed there were nobles like the one whipping Big Sister and the others, and now Itsuki himself, and there were also nobles who instead released their “prey” within their territory to hunt them down for sport.

In other words, Father and the others had been right, and Itsuki had been wrong. It was Father who had seen things clearly, while Itsuki had only been shown whatever suited a comfortable narrative… no, it was more that seeing things that way had simply been more convenient for his own naive sense of justice, Itsuki realized.

But no matter how much he regretted it now, it was too late. He was the very one who had brushed aside and rejected the pleas of Shield Hero and his subordinate, Rabbit Guy—the very hope those people clung to.
And then, an incident occurred that finally broke the cycle of torment Itsuki had been enduring day after day.
